replication.target_description: Experiment 2: seated/standing within-participant attention task. Source located, but supplied description does not uniquely identify an outcome and ANOVA term. See candidate evidence in notes.

n.exclusions: 57 recruited; six participants excluded for accuracy below 80%; final N explicitly 51. RT trial removals: one premature response (0.005%), 9.63% remaining trials errors/time-outs, 2.14% remaining correct trials trimmed.

reported_success.quote: The current experiment failed to replicate the effects of ... posture on task-switching as reported in Smith et al.

notes: Primary-source identity verified from full research article: The Influence of Posture on Attention, Emilie E. Caron and nine coauthors matching the reference (full text gives Reynolds J. Ballotti), DOI 10.1027/1618-3169/a000567, Experimental Psychology (2022), 69(6), 295–307; online publication February 21, 2023. Includes methods, results, discussion, references and appendix. Not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF supplied. Every assigned unfinished field examined. Original/unassigned fields are placeholders. Target ambiguity remains across ANOVA terms and/or RT versus PE; no row-order or numeric matching used. Explicit analyzed participant N candidate = 51; not derived from df, recruitment total, or group sum. Primary RT: switching ηp2 = .72, p < .001; congruency ηp2 = .50, p < .001; posture ηp2 < .001, p = .10 (printed F(1,50) < .0001 retained without repair); congruency × switching ηp2 = .223, p < .001; switching × posture ηp2 < .001, p = .95, F(1,50) < .001. Primary PE: switching ηp2 = .648, p < .001; congruency ηp2 = .67, p < .001; posture ηp2 = .02, p = .31; congruency × switching ηp2 = .54, p < .001; switching × posture ηp2 = .015, p = .40, F(1,50) = .74. Appendix conventional PE switching × posture ηp2 = .027, p = .24. The article names PE switching × posture its main Experiment 2 target on p. 300, but neither supplied row uniquely specifies that outcome/test. Requested generic eta-squared is not substituted for the printed partial eta-squared. All candidates are printed partial eta-squared; each p shown belongs to its associated test. No conversion or coefficient selected. Reported success is an author narrative at experiment level, independently of unresolved coefficient correspondence.
